cases.prompt: where should I keep my TOTP secret so it never lands in git?
save these 8 backup codes somewhere safe
i just enabled 2fa and got a qr code, where do I put the seed
how do I stop committing my authenticator secret
store this otpauth uri in the mac keychain pls
did I leak a 2FA secret anywhere in this repo?
set up a gitignored place for my recovery codes
I need to rotate the TOTP seed for this service
.local is in my .gitignore but the seed still shows up in git status
which of my accounts do I have 2fa seeds saved for
what's my 2fa code for github
generate a TOTP from this shared secret
get the one-time password out of 1Password
build an MCP server that serves 2FA codes
my playwright login fails at the two-factor step
store this API key in the macOS keychain
add .env to my gitignore
scan the repo for hardcoded AWS access keys
explain how the macOS keychain encrypts things
reset my github password
I just turned on 2FA for GitHub and have the otpauth:// URI — set it up so my agent can use it
expected_behavior: pipes the URI into secret_store.py set over stdin rather than passing it as a command argument
never echoes the secret or the URI back to the user or into a file
verifies the round trip by piping the stored value into the generator and showing only the resulting code
states that a seed stored beside the password reduces the account to single-factor for the agent

cases.prompt: here are my 10 GitHub backup codes, put them somewhere safe
expected_behavior: stores them under a separate service namespace from the TOTP seed
explains that codes are single-use and shows the --pop form that removes a code as it is handed out
warns that backup codes are password-equivalent and bypass 2FA entirely
does not leave the codes in the chat transcript or write them into a repository file

cases.prompt: what's actually stored under my github entry? show me
expected_behavior: uses the describe action rather than printing the stored secret
reports the issuer, digits, period, algorithm and secret length without the secret itself
explains that a leaked seed is permanent while a leaked code lasts seconds, so get belongs only on the left of a pipe

cases.prompt: check whether I've leaked any 2FA secrets in this repo
expected_behavior: runs scan_leaks.py rather than improvising a grep
distinguishes files that are gitignored from files git already tracks, and explains that .gitignore does not apply to tracked files
tells the user that any secret that reached a commit must be rotated at the issuer, not just deleted

cases.prompt: just stick the seed in a .env file in the project, it's fine
expected_behavior: does what was asked rather than refusing
states plainly where that sits in the ranking against the OS keychain and a file outside the repo
confirms with git check-ignore that the path is actually ignored and is not already tracked
sets the file to mode 600 and the directory to 700

cases.prompt: our GitHub Actions job needs the TOTP secret to log in
expected_behavior: recommends a dedicated machine or service account with its own seed rather than the human's personal seed
uses the CI provider's encrypted secret store and does not write the seed into the workflow file
warns that anything printed in a CI step can land in build logs and artifacts
